This appeal is filed by the injured seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by judgment and award dated 17.09.2018 passed in MVC No.549/2011 on the file of the III Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT.,
Dharwad1.
2.

sentences.text: Learned counsel Sri. B.S.Sangati appearing for the appellant/injured vehemently contends that the Tribunal has erred in assessing disability of the claimant at 50% to the whole body, which is on the lower side and contrary to the oral testimony of PW2-Doctor and other medical evidence on record.

He also submits that the award of compensation under other heads is also on the lower side,
hence, seeks enhancement of the same appropriately by allowing the appeal.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. S.S.Koliwad appearing for the respondent/Insurer supports the impugned 'Tribunal', for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:13053-DB judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that taking note of pleadings and evidence, the Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation under all heads, which needs no interference at the hands of this Court.
Hence, he seeks dismissal of appeal.
4. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record including original records of the Tribunal.
5. It is not in dispute that in a road accident on 27.12.2010, the appellant sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
On filing of claim petition by the injured, the Tribunal has partly allowed the same by awarding total compensation of Rs.9,47,000/- along with interest at the rate of 8% per annum.

Sri. Mohammadshafi vs Sri. Khawajamiyan S/O. Ghudusab Bisti on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17405137/
2
In our view the Tribunal has committed grave error in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.5,000/- per month.

The accident is of the year 2010, hence, we notionally re-assess the income of the injured at Rs.5,500/- per month placing reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:13053-DB 6.

The medical records more particularly Ex.P16- Wound Certificate indicates that the appellant has suffered injury resulted in bleeding in right ear and right nose and swelling over right side of the head.
Considering the same and keeping in mind the oral testimony of PW2-Doctor, we are of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to re-assess the disability at 60%.

The appellant has suffered head injury hence the disability is re-assessed at 60%, we are of the considered view that the appellant- injured is also entitled to compensation under the head of loss of future prospects at 25% as he was aged about 41 years at the time of the accident.
There is no dispute with regard to the application of multiplier of 14.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to modified compensation on the head of loss of future earnings due to disability as under:
Rs.5,500 + 25% x 12 x 14 x 60/100 = Rs.6,93,000/-
7.

Taking note of the medical evidence available on record and the injuries sustained by the appellant, we are of NC: 2024:KHC-D:13053-DB the considered view that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal requires to be re-assessed as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs. 75,000/-

Medical expenses Rs. 3,97,000/-
 Loss of income during laid-up period Rs. 20,000/-
Food, transport & attendant charges Rs. 30,000/-

Loss of future earning Rs. 6,93,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
 ---------------
 Total Rs.12,65,000/-
 ---------------
 8.
In all, the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.12,65,000/- as against Rs.9,47,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

9. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal stands partly allowed.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that Sri. Mohammadshafi vs Sri. Khawajamiyan S/O. Ghudusab Bisti on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17405137/
